# Host-only upgrade acceptance — 2026-10-31

Current contract supersedes descendant-death requirements in the historical reports here. Upgrade verifies independently identified DB-writing hosts, sends host TERM, allows grace, revalidates before KILL, and verifies host exit before backup. No descendant STOP/signals or descendant-death prerequisite. Workers, shared model hosts, and external tools may survive. Independent writer uncertainty still refuses.

Argv classification now mirrors ordinary server entry modes: bare, `agent`, `--server`, `development-host`, and embedded `--mcp`. `--mcp --grpc-addr ADDRESS` is a client, not an embedded writer. Classification alone grants no signal authority: native discovery still verifies kernel image/start identity and owned listener. Unknown options fail closed. Native multiple-host tests cover bare/server/embedded MCP in addition to agent; unit cases cover external MCP.

## Safety, cleanup, limits

Combined cleanup reports `{}` remaining owned identities and replacement-generation cleanup `[]`; compiled A/B cleanup reports `[]`. Cleanup is distinct from upgrade: it may terminate owned disposable children after root-qualified command/start-time identity checks, or reap directly spawned children; external tool fixtures self-expire. No ambient inventory shutdown or live DB/config/credentials/models used. Synthetic providers and private state only. Evidence and ignored fixture binaries remain for inspection; no merge/push/deployment.

These are bounded Darwin native fixtures and tagged compiled synthetic-provider acceptance, not proof about arbitrary third-party writers. Full package runs do not automatically enable every expensive opt-in gate; the requested compiled A/B and combined paths were run explicitly. The prior unknown-child assertion failure described in execution history is not reproduced in this full passing run. Historical descendant-stop evidence is retained only as history, not an active requirement.
